reference.title: Depression initial-treatment alternatives — dated ACP reference

citation.title: Nonpharmacologic and Pharmacologic Treatments of Adults in the Acute Phase of Major Depressive Disorder: A Living Clinical Guideline From the American College of Physicians
citation.locator: Recommendations 1a and 1b; recommendation text inspected in ACP's public clinical-information index and indexed publication abstract

reference.quote: ACP recommends monotherapy with either cognitive behavioral therapy or a second-generation antidepressant as initial treatment
reference.paraphrase: For adults with an acute moderate-to-severe MDD episode, the dated recommendations support CBT or an SGA alone, with their combination a conditional alternative.
reference.evidence_limitations: Restricted to initial treatment of the specified MDD population. A condition label does not establish current episode, severity, safety or treatment history. This is not an anxiety-treatment or treatment-resistance mapping. ACP lists a March 2026 update; its full text was unavailable, so change reconciliation is pending.

questions.question: Does dated clinical assessment establish adult acute moderate-to-severe MDD, rather than relying on historical condition labels, and is this an initial-treatment decision?

Has a qualified clinician assessed current symptoms, immediate safety needs, differential diagnosis, comorbidities, medication interactions, prior treatment and monitoring needs before considering these options?
What benefits, harms, treatment burden and costs matter to this patient, which option do they prefer, and has service-specific consent been confirmed?
Can the patient access an appropriately qualified CBT clinician, prescribing clinician and follow-up, with suitable language, schedule, travel or technology support?
Do exact patient plan terms, psychotherapy and medication benefits, provider participation and buyer capabilities support each proposed component?
Has an appropriate reviewer reconciled the March 2026 ACP update and any later changes before using these dated recommendations at this decision date?

evidence.population: Adults in an acute moderate-to-severe MDD episode considering initial treatment. This patient's fit is unresolved.
evidence.comparison: CBT alone, a second-generation antidepressant alone, or both
evidence.benefit_summary: Recommendation 1a supports either monotherapy (strong, moderate certainty); 1b suggests the combination (conditional, low certainty). These grades do not rank benefits for this patient.
evidence.harm_summary: Discuss potential harms, adverse effects and treatment burden with an appropriate clinician; no comparative harm rates were extracted.
evidence.limitations: No severity, indication, failure of prior care or safe medication choice follows from a label. CBT is a specific intervention, not any behavioral service. Delivery formats are operational proposals, not a claim of clinical equivalence. No drug or dose is selected.
evidence.quantitative_evidence_status: No numerical benefit or harm estimate extracted; this recommendation comparison does not calculate absolute effects, NNT, ranking or individualized benefit.

alternatives.label: Cognitive behavioral therapy alone
delivery_questions: Is the proposed service actually structured CBT delivered by an appropriately qualified clinician?
Are attendance, language, treatment burden and follow-up arrangements suitable?

alternatives.label: Second-generation antidepressant alone
delivery_questions: Who can assess, prescribe and monitor treatment and discuss adverse effects and interactions?
Are the exact medication benefit, dispensing access and follow-up arrangements established?

alternatives.label: CBT plus a second-generation antidepressant
delivery_questions: Does the proposed arrangement actually provide both CBT and medication management?
How will clinicians coordinate monitoring, preferences, burden and access for both components?
